title: How Pieter Levels runs a solo app portfolio: scrappy shipping, vanilla PHP and AI-assisted code
summary: In a fireside with Balaji, Pieter Levels explains how he maintains Nomad List, Photo AI and other apps nearly alone. He favors scrappy, fast shipping on a stable vanilla PHP stack, with AI coding help, and builds features that solve real nomad pain. The rest of the talk covers digital nomad stats and network state debate.

principles.text: Keep things scrappy and ship fast, but never cut corners on security when you hold user data.
principles.quote: generally uh I like to keep it Scrappy and like to ship fast

principles.text: Pick a boring, stable stack (vanilla PHP) so little changes and maintenance stays low; improve it slowly.
principles.quote: because it's PHP and it's vanilla cult um nothing really changes

principles.text: Lean on AI coding tools like Cursor to write more of the code as a solo builder.
principles.quote: I use cursor a lot like I use a lot of AI stuff now to write codes

principles.text: Data-heavy products can be cheap to maintain: refresh from public sources on a yearly cadence.
principles.quote: you don't need to update a lot like you update every year for example you get new data from World bank right or IMF

principles.text: Build proactive features that solve a painful, specific problem, like tax-liability alerts for travelers.
principles.quote: I send my robot sends you a message if you uh become tax liable in the next 30 days in a country because you add your Trips N list

principles.text: Mine your own user base for data to understand your audience and publish it as a feature.
principles.quote: I have all these users and they do a lot of things they talk to each other they do meetups um and I have one statistics page
